title: Club sandwich on wheat, with cheese

content.title: About
content.content: A club sandwich on wheat bread with cheese consists of three layers of toasted wheat bread, stacked with ham, turkey, bacon, lettuce, tomato and melted cheese. It is served cold or lightly warmed, often cut into halves or quarters.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The club sandwich originated in the United States in the early 1900s and quickly became a staple in diners and cafés.
Traditional recipes use three types of meat, while vegetarian versions replace them with plant‑based alternatives.
Wheat bread gives the sandwich a softer texture compared with white or whole‑grain breads.
Melted cheese is chosen for its ability to bind the ingredients together and add a creamy flavor.
Club sandwiches are commonly served with French fries and pickles on the side.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: The meat layers (ham, turkey, bacon) and cheese provide a substantial amount of complete protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Provides calcium
items.content: Cheese is a good source of calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and wheat bread supply B1, B2, B6 and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Wheat bread and fresh vegetables (lettuce, tomato) add fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Iron
items.content: The meat components deliver heme iron, which is more readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Ham, bacon and cheese are often salty, which can be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Bacon and processed cheese are rich in saturated fats that may raise cholesterol when consumed in excess.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger allergic reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat bread contains gluten, making the sandwich unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of the combination of bread, meat and cheese, the sandwich is relatively high in calories, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is usually cut into quarters and served with fries, a side salad or a dipping sauce. It can be eaten cold or briefly warmed in the oven to melt the cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep a prepared sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. For longer storage, separate the components: keep bread and vegetables apart to prevent sogginess.
